node.label: Jackson Lears
node.date_label: No Place of Grace (1981) · Fables of Abundance (1994) · Something for Nothing: Luck in America (2003)
node.description: A cultural historian of the United States whose work connects religious longing, commercial persuasion and the making of meaning. In his written exchange with B. R. Cohen he explains cultural history as an inquiry into meanings formed through lived anxieties and desires, including unintended consequences. Advertising is examined through trust and confidence as well as sales. His conversation with David Serlin describes chance and control as intertwined practices rather than mutually exclusive eras, linking gambling, belief and economic life without claiming that calculation eliminates uncertainty.
